claim: For the quartic Kolmogorov family printed as equation (3) by Du and Huang, with real parameters \(a,b,A_{10},B_{10}\), the line \(y=1\) contains exactly three positive equilibria \(E_1=(1,1)\), \(E_m=(3/2,1)\), and \(E_2=(2,1)\), because \(P(x,1)=0\) and \(Q(x,1)=(x-1)(x-2)(2x-3)\). The middle equilibrium is parameter independent and has Jacobian \(J(E_m)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-19/16\\-1/2&13/6\end{pmatrix}\), determinant \(-19/32\), and eigenvalues \((26\pm\sqrt{1018})/24\); hence it is a hyperbolic saddle for every parameter choice and cannot undergo a local bifurcation within this family. Thus the published description of model (3) as having two positive equilibrium points omits an unavoidable interior saddle. This result does not assert that these are the only positive equilibria off the line \(y=1\), and it does not by itself invalidate the source’s local focal-value calculations at \((1,1)\) and \((2,1)\).
integrity: The printed vector field was inspected in the primary full text. The line factorization, three Jacobians, saddle determinant, and exact eigenvalues are reproduced by an embedded symbolic checker. Related quartic Kolmogorov literature was compared at the vector-field and equilibrium-configuration level. No independent audit or external validation is claimed.
limitations: The theorem classifies the three positive equilibria on the invariant algebraic line \(y=1\) but does not exclude additional positive equilibria off that line, and it does not recompute the local focal values or small-cycle bifurcations at the two equilibria analyzed in the source.
title: An unavoidable third positive saddle in a quartic Kolmogorov family
